title: Research: audit PR #2530's dirty-lender handoff cuts and recovery movement windows
head: a0565b53edf2f337661b0b9621d478ce327479a9
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds `research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit/`, a code-disjoint finite audit of
PR2530's eight new source-partner aliases and a scoped recovery-movement
certificate. Both frozen forward provider words put the intended original
dirty input in each new lender at handoff. Exact forward row replay and a
separate backward substitution agree on all sixteen observations, with 646
independent initial inputs per provider.

The seven fixed recovery blocks have **1,161 individual legal placements per
provider** in their maximal connected intervals under adjacent commutation
and unchanged incident frames: `11, 9, 8, 10, 272, 406, 445`. These are not a
joint schedule count or a global retiming optimum. Every crossed event and
both interval boundaries have explicit certificates. The source-68 left
boundary is algebraically movable but needs an extra frame climb; several
right boundaries change the actual four-dimensional subspace without changing
its dimension.

The certificate also records that older lenders 4 and 12 hold the mixtures
`(x4-x68)/2` and `x12+x31`. The new-lender original-input invariant must not be
generalized to all older aliases.

This is a finite certificate and scoped proof, not a new helper inventory,
physical schedule, supplier or κ. Native inverse-transpose implementations,
Gaussian phases, final cleanup and target endpoint, buffer stock, full rank
invoice, owners, global/outer admission, precision and all-size/compiler
obligations are not recertified. The selected frontier is unchanged.

## Task and overlap

The claim is in [discussion #2606](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2606).
Full local task metadata and refresh evidence are in `TASK.json`.

Task card:

* **Task ID / scope key:** `independent-moment` / `c191650c0fa8d2fa514e`, refined to
  `PR2530/eight-source-partners/chronological-lender-cuts/both-words/exact-rational-independent-audit`.
* **Base / exact predecessors:** main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`;
  PR2530 `b4012098048e12500b2d33d2e84be281915a27ac`; its PR2462 supplier
  `ef34071fee6dfb0286e9850a5cec4e36d9eb126d`.
* **Concrete question:** do all eight new lenders hold their intended original
  inputs at their actual handoffs, and what fixed-block recovery movements
  preserve the complete B map without a frame change?
* **Scope status / reason:** refined. The card permits independent source-ledger
  reconstruction. The new lifetime implication and explicit cut certificates
  add coverage beyond another evaluation of an already checked moment root.
* **Audited claim:** PR2530's recovery-before-destructive-handoff assertion.
  The source construction is unchanged; the movement model is declared above.
* **Method / domain:** exact rationals and formal invertible operator words;
  both frozen forward providers, all eight named new lenders, seven fixed
  recovery blocks, nine recovery operations, explicit `F_2^9` frame sets.
* **Nearest overlap:** PR2530 supplies the construction and full author checks;
  PR2571/PR2575 change owner packing; PR2588 changes helper labels/frame charges;
  PR2573's exhaustion excludes source-partner recovery; PR2315 audits an older
  borrow43 record and buffer accounting. Discussion #2612 searches new source
  assignments. This package holds PR2530 fixed and audits its intermediate
  source values and recovery movement.
* **Budget / observable improvement:** audit only; no new cost or κ target.
  Require exact boundary witnesses and explicit semantic/frame failure controls.
* **Success / falsification / cap:** complete sixteen handoff identities and
  fourteen movement intervals, or a concrete failing cut. One bounded session;
  no unrestricted synthesis or complete supplier replay.
* **Predecessor authors / artifact:** zxv, Jeremy Kothe, Tekalign, Vlado
  Vojdanovski, Cinna Davis and retained lineage; the package above, reproduced
  with `python3 -I -B research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit/verify.py`.

At the final refresh, canonical main, priority revision 4, the selected record
and PR2530's exact head were unchanged. The final offline snapshot covered 812
open PRs at 16:22:35 UTC and 1,276 Discussion records at 16:27:10 UTC on
2026-10-15, both with complete pagination. The changed-file snapshot was from
15:59:04 UTC and flagged PR2571's file list as truncated beyond 100 files.
The later PR2621 timing/hosting claim was also screened as context, not audited
or used as a source. These searches are overlap evidence, not proof of novelty. Exact timestamp
and pins are in `TASK.json`.

## Validation

On Linux, CPython 3.12.3, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit/test_verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit --check-only
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-source-partner-cut-audit
```

The registered replay runs the optimized verifier and focused test file. It
passes `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`; all five tests pass (8.096 seconds
for the final focused file). The verifier prints:

```text
PASS_T74_SOURCE_PARTNER_CUT_AUDIT providers=2 handoffs=16 recovery_gates=18 reverse_cuts=16 movement_windows=14 semantic_rejections=24 no_new_kappa
```

Validation includes exact input SHA-256/Git-blob pins, canonical certificate
comparison, noncommutative positive fixtures, 24 rejecting recovery/sign/order/
handoff controls, full 646-column B-map replay of all 28 interval endpoints,
and 28 immediately outside placements that fail map-plus-zero-climb
preservation. Two outside placements preserve the algebraic map and fail only
the frame condition. A target-only prelude corruption deliberately still passes
the lender-cut check and changes the full B map, documenting its coverage limit.

The predecessor's generator and checker were inspected but never imported or
executed. Normal replay does not write package files. No full native/global/
outer cold replay, formal-kernel proof, hosted CI or independent human review
is claimed.

## Open next questions

The README and `TASK.json` give two bounded follow-ups: bind prescribed
invertible-mixture lender rows to their complete compensation/cleanup contracts,
starting with older roles 4 and 12; or supply exact inverse rows and an available
frame for one three-source recovery candidate before attempting a new word.
Neither source availability nor an algebraically movable block establishes a
favorable native bill or supplier admission.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The intermediate-cut audit exposed a useful distinction between algebraic
movement and frame-preserving movement without launching a full record replay.
Future recovery constructions could publish a small table of restored rows,
the last required reads and the first destructive handoffs beside their endpoint
receipts. That would make the next independent review more direct.
